speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I can see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with recent fever, headache, and rhinorrhea. To help me understand the progression, have you noticed any specific patterns to the rash, such as it spreading from your face downward or appearing in crops? Also, have you experienced any joint pain or swelling recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description; the progression from a prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea to a facial rash sparing the nose is very suggestive of a specific viral exanthem. Has she been exposed to anyone with similar symptoms recently, and does she have any history of atopy or asthma? Also, please tell me if she has developed any swollen lymph nodes, particularly around her neck.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The clinical picture of a high-fever prodrome followed by a rash that appears as the fever subsides, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy mentioned, is classic for HHV-6 infection in a pediatric patient. No further tests are required for this diagnosis.
